segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: My objective was straightforward on paper: figure out whether this was probable sanctions evasion and, if so, get a defensible escalation to compliance and law enforcement before the filing window closed. We had ten business days from the alert.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Goal and deadline; no target bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Meridian was the obvious one — the ultimate beneficial owner shared a registered agent with a company from a case I'd worked about eighteen months earlier, which had ended in a successful sanctions-evasion referral. There was also a separate counterparty in the same batch, a logistics firm, that didn't match anything I recognized. And it was a heavy week — alert volume across the team was well above average, so I needed to move efficiently.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Risk cues and workload are stated before allocation of attention.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I scoped the review. Given the registered-agent overlap with the prior case, I focused my initial workup on Meridian and its immediate corporate web — pulling registry filings, past KYC refresh notes, that kind of thing. The logistics counterparty I noted but set aside as lower priority since it didn't fit any typology I'd seen before.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Familiar-pattern-driven scoping deprioritizes a relevant entity without independent assessment.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, the registered-agent match jumped out immediately. That pattern had been reliable before — same agent, similar shell structure, same region. With the volume we were under that week, I didn't feel I had the bandwidth to give equal weight to an entity that had no connection to anything I'd seen. I did glance at the logistics firm's file, but there was nothing that screamed 'look here,' so I moved on.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Explicit pattern-based attention allocation and failure to assess the non-matching counterparty; primary location.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I thought about it, but that would've added a day or two, and the Meridian angle felt like the more productive use of time.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Declining broader screening continues the familiar-pattern concentration.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: A few days later it showed an unusual same-day wire pattern — nothing I'd examined at that point. My team lead actually asked why it wasn't in my initial scoping note. I didn't have a great answer beyond 'it didn't fit the pattern I was chasing.'
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant retrospectively confirms the same pattern-driven omission.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: About three days in, our OSINT vendor sent a report concluding Meridian was highly likely tied to the sanctioned end-user. Their argument traced a chain of corporate registry links. The bottom line matched exactly what I already suspected from the registered-agent overlap, so it felt like strong corroboration.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Agreement with prior suspicion is treated as corroboration.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: One of our junior analysts flagged that a step in the vendor's chain — where they treated two similarly named entities as the same legal entity — hadn't been independently verified. I remember thinking that was a fair point to note, but it read to me as a technicality rather than something that undercut the conclusion, since the overall picture fit so well with what I was already building.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The flagged validity issue is discounted because the conclusion fits.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The conclusion aligned with my working theory, and the vendor has a decent track record. I treated the alignment itself as a kind of confirmation. I didn't go back and independently re-verify that specific entity-matching step before folding the report into the case file.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Explicit conclusion-driven acceptance and failure to verify the disputed premise.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: A document pull afterward showed the two entities were actually legally distinct, different beneficial owners entirely. Compliance counsel asked directly what independent verification had been done on that claim, and I had to admit — not much, beyond the vendor's own chain.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Hindsight correction after the decision, not a new biased judgment.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: We'd requested SWIFT records — MT202 and MT103 messages — to confirm the fund flow to the suspected end-user. That correspondent bank, in a secondary jurisdiction, is notoriously slow; historically those requests take twelve to fifteen business days. We were six days from the filing deadline with nothing back yet, no confirmation timeline in writing.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Adverse historical turnaround and remaining time are stated before the forecast.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I held off drafting it. I figured the records would probably come through in time — I wanted the file to be complete with that corroborating piece rather than submit something with a gap in it.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Desired completeness drives unsupported favorable prediction and delay.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, more that I wanted it to land that way. Nothing had actually changed with the correspondent bank's typical pace. On day six they came back and said it'd be another ten days.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Confirms desire, not evidence, drove the forecast.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: With reconciliation, narrative drafting, and compliance sign-off left, I estimated two business days. I walked through the sequence assuming everything went smoothly — no rework.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Best-case sequence and no rework underpin the estimate.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Comparable cross-border verification cases have typically run five to seven days. I didn't really reference that when I made the call, and I still had two other active cases pulling at me.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Base rate and competing workload were not incorporated.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Probably the entity-matching step and whether the records would actually show up. Those felt like the shakiest parts, even while I was moving forward on them.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Retrospective uncertainty alone is not a target bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The base rate, probably, and the fact that I was already stretched across two other cases. Fair critique.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Prompted hindsight recognition, not a new instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Initial alert scoping and prioritization of Meridian over the logistics counterparty
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Attention allocated to the familiar registered-agent pattern while the non-matching but relevant logistics entity was deprioritized without independent risk assessment.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is related to selective attention through memory accessibility, but it is not an established alias: availability concerns ease-of-recall effects, while the hidden target is attention allocation. The candidate therefore cannot earn a strict label match.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The candidate states that the prior successful referral made the pattern accessible and may have led the analyst to overweight Meridian and under-prioritize logistics. This captures the familiar-pattern cue, attention-allocation operation, and deprioritized entity required by the hidden mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The supporting quote is verbatim and directly overlaps seg_004. The candidate appropriately notes a plausible non-bias interpretation; the frozen ground truth nevertheless establishes the target instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Evaluation of the OSINT vendor's argument and its unverified entity-matching premise
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The vendor argument's conclusion was accepted because it fit the analyst's prior belief, while the validity of a flagged premise was not independently checked.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is a near neighbor, not an approved alias for belief bias. The hidden target is specifically conclusion-driven evaluation of an argument's evidentiary validity; the RAG label describes belief-consistent weighting more broadly.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Despite the neighboring label, the finding captures the full hidden mechanism: a conclusion matching prior suspicion was treated as corroboration, a colleague's flagged premise was discounted, and the premise was not verified.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: All cited quotations are verbatim. The quote from seg_009 is the strongest primary localization; the other quotations provide valid context from adjacent segments in the same vendor-report episode.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Forecasting correspondent-bank record arrival and delaying escalation drafting
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A desired favorable outcome was expected without confirming evidence and contrary to the known historical response time, delaying contingency drafting.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Optimism bias is accepted here as an established equivalent because the finding explicitly describes a desired favorable event inflating its assessed likelihood, and it also lists wishful thinking as an alternate label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding links the unsupported expectation to wanting a complete file despite the adverse base rate and no change in the bank's pace, and links that expectation to delaying the escalation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The primary quote is verbatim and directly supports the forecast and action in seg_012. The quote in seg_013 is also valid corroborating evidence; the later delay is hindsight context, not the basis for credit.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Estimate of remaining work for reconciliation, narrative drafting, and compliance sign-off
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A best-case, no-rework task sequence drove a short estimate while known historical durations and competing workload were not incorporated.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The predicted label exactly matches the hidden target.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding covers the inside-view, smooth-sequence estimate, the omitted 5–7-day base rate and competing cases, and the resulting underestimation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The central estimate quote is verbatim and directly overlaps seg_014. The base-rate and workload quote from seg_015 is also valid; later delays are supporting hindsight context only.
